turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hi, thanks for coming in today. What's been going on for you lately?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It's been a whirlwind, to be honest. I feel like I've been on top of the world lately. I've been working on this new project and I'm really starting to see where it's going. I mean, I've barely slept in a few days and I was thinking, "Why not? I'm feeling great!" I've never felt so productive in my life.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: You seem really energized and motivated about this project. What is it about this project that's got you so excited? And how are you taking care of yourself to keep this momentum going?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: The project! It's just everything, you know? I mean, the possibilities are endless and I feel like I'm on the cusp of something huge. I've already started making connections with investors and I'm sure it's just going to take off. And as for taking care of myself... well, to be honest, I don't really need as much sleep as everyone else does. I've never felt more clear-headed and focused. I'm just going with it, you know?

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I can hear the enthusiasm in your voice. That's really inspiring. It sounds like this project is bringing you a lot of joy and a sense of purpose. Can you tell me a bit more about what this project means to you? What are you hoping to achieve with it?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (suddenly getting slightly defensive) Oh, it's not just about the project, okay? It's about the feeling I get when I'm working on it. I feel alive, you know? Like I'm finally doing something that matters. And as for what I'm hoping to achieve... well, I'm hoping to change the game, obviously. (laughs) I mean, why settle for just being good when you can be great? And I'm not just talking about this project, I'm talking about my whole life. I'm on a roll and I don't want to slow down.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: You seem to be really proud of yourself and your accomplishments. That's great. It sounds like this project is giving you a sense of identity and purpose. I want to acknowledge that it takes a lot of courage to pursue your passions like this. Can you tell me more about what it feels like to be "on a roll" right now? What does that look like for you?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (irritated) Look, I don't see why you're making such a big deal out of this. It's just me being successful, okay? It's not like I'm hurting anyone. And as for what it feels like... it's just exhilarating, that's all. I'm on cloud nine, and I don't want to come down. I'm making more money than I ever thought possible, and I'm meeting new people all the time. It's like the whole world is opening up for me. (starts to speed up) And I'm not going to let anyone or anything bring me down, not even you...

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: (empathetically) I hear that you're feeling really empowered and in control right now. It takes a lot of confidence to say that. But I also want to make sure we're talking about this in a way that feels safe and comfortable for you. Can I check in with you about how you're feeling, just to make sure we're on the same page? (pauses) I want to make sure you're not feeling overwhelmed or too much pressure to keep this pace up.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (irritated, slightly agitated) Overwhelmed? Pressure? No, I'm fine. I'm just... I'm just feeling really good, okay? And you're starting to make me feel like there's something wrong with that. Like I'm doing something wrong. (pauses, takes a deep breath) Look, I just need to keep moving forward. I need to keep pushing. And if you're not willing to support me in that, then maybe we're not a good fit. (starts to speed up again) I mean, what's the point of even trying if someone's just going to bring me down?

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: (calmly) I'm here to support you, and I'm not trying to bring you down. I want to make sure we're on the same page, that's all. Can I try something? I want to acknowledge that it sounds like you're feeling a lot of drive and motivation right now. And I'm here to help you explore what that means for you, without putting any pressure on you. Can I try to reframe what we're talking about in a way that feels more collaborative and supportive?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (still slightly agitated, but starting to calm down) Fine. Yeah, sure. Try it. (crosses arms, still looking a bit skeptical) But don't expect me to change my mind or anything. I'm just curious to see how you're going to spin this.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: (empathetically) Okay. Let's take a step back and look at this project as something that's bringing you a lot of joy and fulfillment. That's something to be proud of! And I'm here to support you in exploring what that means for you. Can we talk about what you need from me right now? Do you want to explore ways to maintain this momentum, or do you want to talk about any challenges you're facing in this process?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (slightly more open, but still guarded) I guess I just want to keep moving forward. I don't want to slow down. But... (pauses, looks away) I don't know, it's just hard to talk about this stuff. I feel like everyone's always trying to bring me down, or tell me I'm doing something wrong. (looks back at the therapist) Can you just promise me you're not going to do that? Can you just listen to me and support me, without trying to fix me or tell me what to do?

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: (empathetically) I promise you, I'm here to listen and support you. I'm not here to fix you or tell you what to do. I'm here to support you in exploring what you want and need. Can I just check in with you about one thing? I want to make sure we're not pushing too hard on any sensitive topics. Are you feeling okay to talk about some of the challenges you're facing in this process?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looking slightly uncomfortable) Challenges? I don't know... I mean, I'm not really thinking about challenges. I'm just thinking about the future, and all the possibilities. (pauses, looks away) But if you must know, sometimes I do get a little... (pauses again, looking for the right words) ...frazzled. Yeah, that's it. Frazzled. It's like my brain is moving faster than my body can keep up, and it gets hard to focus. But that's just part of the price of being this successful, right? (looks back at the therapist, a hint of defensiveness creeping in)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: You're sharing with me that sometimes you feel frazzled and overwhelmed. That's a really honest thing to admit. And I'm here to support you in exploring what that means for you. Can I try to offer some support? Would you like to talk about some strategies for managing stress and overwhelm, or would you like to explore other topics first?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (getting slightly agitated again) Strategies? No, no, I don't need strategies. I just need to keep pushing forward. I don't have time to worry about feeling frazzled or overwhelmed. I've got too much to do, too much to achieve. (pauses, takes a deep breath) And another thing, what's wrong with feeling frazzled and overwhelmed? Isn't that just part of being successful? (looks at the therapist with a hint of accusation) Are you saying I'm not successful because I feel frazzled and overwhelmed?

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: (empathetically) I'm not saying that at all. I'm just trying to support you in exploring what you're feeling. It takes a lot of courage to admit when we're feeling overwhelmed. Can I try to reframe what we're talking about? You're feeling really driven and motivated, and that's something to be proud of. But it sounds like maybe there's a bit more going on underneath that. Can we explore what that might be?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (getting frustrated) Reframe? You're always trying to reframe everything. Can't you just listen to me without trying to fix me or change the way I think? I'm telling you, I'm fine. I'm just driven. And I don't need some therapist telling me how to feel or what to think. (pauses, takes a deep breath, and tries to calm down) I'm sorry. I just... I don't know, it feels like you're not getting it.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: (empathetically) I'm trying to get it, but I think we might need to take a step back and re-evaluate what we're working on. It sounds like you're feeling really frustrated with me right now, and that's okay. Can we take a break and come back to this conversation later? Maybe we can try to find a better way to work together.
